items.note: City release of 10 July 2020; title correct. CHF 300 -> CHF 780 annual card is a Stadtrat proposal to be decided by the Gemeinderat (correctly framed as proposal). But the page says regular/long-stay overnight parking (Dauerparkieren in der Nacht), previously free, would be put on the same footing as daytime long-stay parking and so become chargeable; it does not say all night-time street parking would be charged at daytime rates.
items.corrected_text: The city executive proposed a revised parking-card ordinance, to be decided by the city parliament, that would raise the annual blue-zone resident card from CHF 300 to CHF 780. Regular overnight parking on public streets, previously free, would be treated like daytime long-stay parking and become chargeable.

items.note: City release of 29 March 2021; title correct. Page: Parkhaus Central, Seilergraben 74, 36 spaces, smallest of the ten municipal garages, closes end of March 2021; high costs and new standards (which would cut spaces after renovation, making cost-covering operation impossible) argue against renovation; the 30 spaces under the 1996 historic parking compromise move to nearby Parkhaus Urania. Draft's reason is simplified (omits the new-standards point) but not wrong.

City release of 1 December 2021; title correct. Voters approved the new communal transport master plan (kommunaler Richtplan Verkehr) on 28 November 2021; it states blue-zone spaces should be reduced; the Stadtrat withdraws the PKV proposal and will draft an adapted version.

SRF, 30.10.2024; title correct. First reading (erste Lesung) in the Gemeinderat; 35-45 Rp/kg fossil, 30-40 Rp/kg zero-emission; only residents without private parking eligible (Bieler Modell); annual fee from CHF 300 to CHF 540.

SRF results page (published 26.09.2025, updated 28.09.2025, vote held 28 September 2025); title correct. PKV yes 52.8%; resident cards to cost two to three times today's price; priced by weight, electric cheaper than petrol; tradespeople may park almost anywhere if there is room.

Suedostschweiz, 14.06.2026; title correct. Over 59% no; SVP initiative (also supported by FDP and Mitte/EVP in parliament); public spaces removable only if same number of public spaces kept in the district; city plans to convert about 9,000-11,000 surface spaces over 10-15 years; the 1990s compromise was terminated by the city executive in 2021.

City release dated 1 April 2026; title correct. Supported: since early 2026 the city runs its ten garages and the Zürich Bus Station itself; PZAG staff and operations now belong to Liegenschaften Stadt Zürich; PZAG founded 2008; nothing changes for customers. Overstated: the page does NOT say PZAG has been dissolved. It says the subsidiary 'wird nun aufgelöst' (is now being dissolved) and, after audited final accounts and Stadtrat approval of project completion, 'kann damit formell aufgelöst werden' (can now be formally dissolved). Also states the move follows a 2022 Gemeinderat motion.
items.corrected_text: Since early 2026, the city's real-estate department (Liegenschaften Stadt Zürich) has run the ten municipal garages and the Zürich Bus Station itself, ending 17 years of outsourcing to Parking Zürich AG (founded 2008). In April 2026 the city said the company could now be formally dissolved, and that nothing changes for customers.

items.note: ACS Zürich press release dated 6 February 2025; title correct. The page says the Gemeinderat approved the Green Party postulate on converting municipal garages into housing (Umnutzung ... in Wohnsiedlungen), and ACS Zürich condemned it. 'other city infrastructure' is not on the page. The postulate is a request to the executive to examine, not a decision to convert.
items.corrected_text: The city parliament approved a Green Party postulate on converting municipal parking garages into housing. The motoring club ACS Zürich, which reported the decision, opposed it.

items.note: Cantonal government decision RRB 129 of 7 February 2024. The 70-150% increase for 2023 is a claim made in the cantonal MPs' question, not confirmed in the government's reply (the reply confirms a fee adjustment and that previous fees were well below market). Reply supports: Irchel garage renovation about CHF 25.6 million (provisional), sustained occupancy (Dauerauslastung) about 70%, 994 long-term rental contracts at 31 Dec 2022 and 220 cancelled by 31 Jan 2023, including cancellations not caused by the fee increase. Item date 2023 refers to the fee change; the document itself is from 2024. Title matches the document heading (numbered '129.').
items.corrected_text: Cantonal MPs stated that the University of Zurich raised its parking fees, including at the Irchel garage, by 70-150% for 2023. The cantonal government's reply says the Irchel renovation cost about CHF 25.6 million, occupancy is about 70%, and 220 of 994 long-term rental contracts were cancelled by end of January 2023, not all because of the fee increase.

items.note: Netzwoche, 14 October 2019; title correct. App payment available for six months; 10% of parking-fee revenue via apps; 505,000 transactions and CHF 1.4 million since start; providers Parkingpay, Easypark, Parknow.
Blick, 31.05.2021; title is the page headline. About 120 public charging stations, one per 41 e-cars; ewz plans more than 20 additional stations in 2021.
TCS 2025 test page; title correct. Zürich top at 73.32% of 8 cities; garages Hohe Promenade, Urania, Messe Zürich and Opéra named; Opéra charging 28 Rappen/kWh but proprietary app required.

City release of 5 June 2023; title correct. Total traffic fell markedly in 2020 and 2021; shift from public transport towards walking, cycling and car; at end of 2022 PT passengers only slightly below end-2019; 2022 cycling counts highest since counting began.

SRF, 28.02.2025; title correct. Jelmoli on Bahnhofstrasse closed 28 February 2025; owner Swiss Prime Site cited retail trends, especially online commerce and declining role of shopping as leisure; Manor to occupy three floors from 2027 after renovation.

corrected_summary: Zurich's city executive proposed a pricier resident parking card in 2020, withdrew it after voters approved a transport master plan calling for fewer blue-zone spaces in November 2021, and voters approved a weight-based resident card in September 2025; in June 2026 voters rejected an initiative to protect parking-space numbers, and the 1990s parking compromise had been ended in 2021. Since early 2026 the city has run its ten municipal garages itself, and in April 2026 it said Parking Zürich AG could now be formally dissolved. Demand-side events include the pandemic drop in traffic in 2020-2021 and the closure of the Jelmoli department store in February 2025.
